newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates close steady, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates close steady, seen stable.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed steady on Thursday amid higher supplies of the new crop from farms, dealers at Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said.
They said the rates were likely to open unchanged on Saturday when the market reopens after Friday's Islamic holiday.
Balanced demand and supply kept the prices unchanged, a dealer at Nasim Usman & Co said.

Higher new-crop supplies to ginneries is likely to ease the prices in the next week, he said. In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 was quoted for 2,340/2,360 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) the K-68 for 2,550/2,570 and the MNH-93 for 2,550/2,565.

The KCA said exporters had shipped 125,515 (375-lb) bales of cotton by June 28 compared to 1.82 million bales in the same time a year ago. Exporters had registered contracts for the export of 164,756 bales by July 8 compared to 2.32 million bales in the same time a year ago.
